LESSON: WRITING 11.4.1 GUIDED WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 11
Topic 11.4: Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing, part of Strand 11 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade two ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to construct sentences correctly? 2) Why is it important to write clearly and legibly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. write down words related to the theme from a dictation.

2. write sentences using the words learnt from prompts with peers.

3. practise writing meaningful sentences.

4. create sentences using regular comparatives and superlatives adjectives, share with peers and give feedback. 1)

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. write down words related to the theme from a dictation.
2. write sentences using the words learnt from prompts with peers.
3. practise writing meaningful sentences.
4. create sentences using regular comparatives and superlatives adjectives, share with peers and give feedback. 1)

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 11.4.1 Guided Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Learning to learn-is enhanced as the learner practises writing meaningful sentences in different context.

Values:
Responsibility as the learner takes initiative to practise writing meaningful sentences.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Life Skills (effective communication)- as the learner creates sentences using regular comparative and superlative sentences.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner uses the writing skills to write clearly and correctly in other writing areas.
